messages:
Jon H.: FYI, saw a silent GPU host failure in us-west-2 during a long-running batch. node gn7-004 stopped heartbeating to controller, kubelet unreachable. No pod termination events in controller logs. :eyes:
Maria L.: Pulling logs now. can you paste dmesg / nvidia output?
Jon H.: pasted snippets below:
```
[   78.4321] pci_bus 0000:06: reported PCIe Bus Error: severity=Corrected, type=Physical Layer, id=0000(Receiver ID)
[  123.9876] NVRM: Xid (PCI:e:0000:06:00): 31, Channel 00000004
kernel: watchdog: GPU hung, resetting...
```
Sam R.: Xid 31 is usually a GPU engine hang / driver reset. but the node stopped responding to kubelet entirely, not just GPU processes. could be a PCI/BIOS level hang.
Ethan K.: Capacity impact: this reduces us-west ded pool by 1/20 GPUs. autoscaler tried to spin up a replacement but tickets show API rate-limited for the last 10m. we should shift some runs to eu-west asap to keep SLAs.
Natalie P.: Agreed. Plan: 1) cordon gn7-004, 2) attempt remote soft-reboot, 3) if unresponsive, RMA and offline, 4) shift traffic/pinned jobs to eu-west fallback. Sam can open cloud hardware ticket.
Jon H.: doing step 1 & 2 now. command I ran: `kubectl cordon gn7-004 && kubectl drain gn7-004 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` (careful: NV cache-backed pods pinned to local SSDs — we excluded them).
Maria L.: I tried remote soft-reboot via BMC; BMC accepted reboot but host never came back (no network). console shows PCI device lost during init.
Sam R.: Opening provider case now, linking to instance id i-0f9a3b2c and BMC session 9876. RMA requested, ETA 72h for hardware swap. Case# CW-34211. tagging support: @support-team.
infra-bot: Incident created: CW-34211 (us-west-2 GPU host failure). Severity: sev3. Affected capacity: -1 ded GPU.
Ethan K.: I'm shifting low-priority batch queues to eu-west and enabling preemptible fallbacks for latency-sensitive routes. Will update routing policy in Console -> Routing -> us-west-fallback to prefer eu-west with 300ms penalty.
Natalie P.: I'll schedule a quick customer notice for any teams with pinned jobs to us-west. Draft: "We detected degraded GPU capacity in us-west-2; short-term failover to eu-west enabled. Replacement ETA ~72h." Send internal ops note to infra-oncall.
Jon H.: Node is still unresponsive; drain finished for non-pinned pods. leaving taint "gpu-outage=true:NoSchedule" on gn7-004.
Maria L.: Collected kernel + nv driver dumps, uploaded to /mnt/ops/gn7-004-dumps.tar.gz and attached to CW-34211. Also captured BMC serial logs.
Sam R.: Provider acknowledged ticket, asked for hardware serial and time of failure. Provided. They escalated to on-site tech.
Ethan K.: Checkpoint: we've shifted 40% of the queue to eu-west, preemptible jobs increased by 2x, and health checks indicate fallbacks healthy. Cost delta estimated +$1.2k/day while at reduced capacity.
Natalie P.: I'll open a short post-incident doc after replacement: include RC steps for PCI hang, BMC reboot checklist, and routing rollback steps.
Jon H.: Thanks all. I'll keep monitoring and update when provider confirms swap. :thumbsup:
